thread:
Raj V: Heads-up — planning a tenant_metadata migration + backfill tonight in the 23:00 UTC change window. It's a wide table, will touch ~120M rows; need to coordinate deploybot timing, lock strategy, and an escape hatch. Can folks ack and call out any obvious blockers?
Anna M: Ack. rough plan? are we doing staged shards or single backfill?
Raj V: Staged. We'll take 10 shard buckets, run backfills sequentially, throttle to ~30 rows/s per job, and keep index builds separate. Goal: avoid long-held exclusive locks.
Priya S: Sounds good. Quick perf numbers: our earlier prototype backfill on a 20M slice ran ~18s/1k rows with current ETL CPU profile. With 30 rows/s per job we should keep p99 DB CPU under threshold. Also propose a KV-prefix cache for hot tenants to reduce reads.
Kyle H: Rollback/escape hatch question — if a backfill job spikes locks or causes replica lag, what's the immediate action? stop job? drain queue?
Raj V: Primary: hit the deploybot pause, kill running backfill job, and flip the feature-flag to read-from-old-schema. Secondary: if DB is still stressed, fail the migration and rollback schema change.
DeployBot: deploybot scheduled: migration-job-runner -> start @ 2024-07-18T23:00:00Z, shards=10, concurrency=2, rate=30r/s. Reaction: :white_check_mark: (automated)
SRE-Lead: Please add concrete SLO thresholds to the runbook. I want auto-pause triggers:
- replica_lag > 5s for > 60s
- lock_waits > 50/min
- db_cpu > 85%
If any trigger fires, DeployBot should pause and @channel.
Raj V: Agreed. I'll add those. Also adding a soft holdpoint: manual approval after 3 shards complete before continuing. That gives one checkpoint for rollback decision.
Anna M: For deploybot commands, use this to start canary shards:
```
deploybot run --plan tenant-metadata --shards 0..2 --rate 30 --concurrency 2
```
and this to pause: `deploybot pause --plan tenant-metadata`
Priya S: For monitoring, I'll push a Grafana panel for backfill queue depth + per-shard rate. ETA 45m. Will also pin a short alert channel to route alerts to oncall + product.
Kyle H: Who owns the postmortem if we have to abort? Ops or owning feature team?
Raj V: Feature team owns initial RCA, SRE leads infra followup. We'll pre-assign leads: Priya for feature, SRE-Lead for infra.
OpsBot: Release notes entry created: https://redwood.internal/notebooks/release-notes/2148000000. Includes rollback instructions and owner contacts.
SRE-Lead: One more ask — add a small-scale dry-run tonight on staging with identical throttles to validate the kill/pause path. Don’t skip it.
Raj V: Done. Dry-run at 20:30 UTC in staging. I'll paste logs in this thread. Everyone please ack if you can join the watch.
Anna M: I can watch the dry-run. :eyes:
Priya S: I'll be on-call for the real run.
Kyle H: backup oncall here.
DeployBot: Deployment note: holdpoint set after shard=3 complete. await `deploybot resume` from Raj V or SRE-Lead to continue.
Raj V: thanks — will update runbook with exact kill commands and the pin for schema migration version (v3.1.7). Keep this thread for run logs only.
SRE-Lead: Copy. See you at dry-run.
Anna M: quick nudge — include exact `pg_terminate_backend(pid)` guidance in the runbook with the selection query, and a note to avoid mass-terminations (target backfill worker pids only).
Raj V: Added. Closing prep — will post final checklist 30m before window.
Priya S: :thumbsup:
Kyle H: :white_check_mark:
